# Resident's restricted amalgamation: acquisition of revenue account property and land ¶20-108

Under s FO 10(6), if property is revenue account property of the amalgamating company but not of the amalgamated company, the consideration for the disposal and acquisition is taken as the market value of the property at the time of the amalgamation. The land will not be held to be revenue account property simply because of the operation of the "bright-line test" or the "2-year rule" in ss CB 6A, CB 9–CB 11, and CB 14.

However, s FO 17(3) may apply.

Land held on capital account by the amalgamating company but on revenue account by the amalgamated company because of the bright-line test or 2-year rule is also deemed to be transferred to the amalgamated company at market value at the time of amalgamation. The transfer of land that is subject to the bright- line test or 2-year rule will not trigger assessability, rather the relevant bright-line or 2-year period will apply from the date of acquisition by the original amalgamating company. Under s FO 17(3), if the amalgamated company subsequently disposes of the property within the relevant bright-line or 2-year period from the date of acquisition of the amalgamating company, any profit or gain from the disposal is income of the amalgamated company.

When, at the time of the amalgamation, it is unclear whether the amalgamated company holds the property on revenue or capital account (eg the amalgamated company would only hold the property on revenue account if it disposed of it within 2 years), the property is transferred at market value when:

## the land is held on revenue account by the amalgamating company (but not merely because of the

bright-line test or 2-year rule), and

## the land is, or may be, revenue account property of the amalgamated company because of the bright-

line test or 2-year rule.

See Table 2 in IS 25/10, "Income tax and GST – Amalgamations" which summarises whether land is transferred at cost or market value on a concessionary amalgamation.

*Refs: s FO 10(6), ss CB 6A, s FO 17(3)*

## Relief from interest limitation rules

## Note: From 1 April 2024, interest deductibility is being restored in a phased manner and, from 1 April

2025, the rules are substantially repealed (¶10-814).

Section DH 5(5)(d) provides rollover relief to a transfer of property as part of a company amalgamation under s FO 17. Relief applies when "disallowed residential property" (s DH 5(2)) passes from an amalgamating company to the amalgamated company on a resident's restricted amalgamation on or after 27 March 2021, provided the amalgamating company had a grandparented transitional loan.

Rollover relief is only available if the amalgamating company and amalgamated company are New Zealand resident and are not treated as non-resident under a tax treaty. This is to ensure that, consistent with the rules for bright-line rollover relief, rollover relief for interest limitation is provided on the condition the property remains within the New Zealand tax base. The amalgamated company's grandparented transitional loan balance may not exceed the amalgamating company's loan balance at the time of transfer.

Law: IT07 ss DH 5(5)(d), FO 10(6), FO 17
